source: The Sayings of the Desert Fathers (Apophthegmata Patrum). Public-domain English translations (Wallis Budge, Helen Waddell). Used as a fallback on Today when the headline saint has no entry in the registry's quotes array. Rotated by day-of-year so the same line does not appear two days running.

sayings.text: I saw the snares of the enemy spread out over the world, and I groaned and said, What can pass through these? And I heard a voice saying, Humility.

cite.searched: No collection of the Sayings of the Desert Fathers is in the app. Budge's public-domain translation (The Paradise of the Holy Fathers, 1907, vol. 2, Book I, ch. 10, no. 453), which the History section quotes (anthony-and-the-desert), words this saying differently.

sayings.text: Our life and our death is with our neighbour. If we win our brother, we win God; if we cause our brother to stumble, we have sinned against Christ.

cite.searched: No collection of the Sayings of the Desert Fathers is in the app to check these words against. Budge's public-domain translation (The Paradise of the Holy Fathers, 1907) is the edition to search; this wording reads like a modern translation.

sayings.text: Whoever has not been tried by temptation cannot enter the Kingdom of Heaven; take away temptations, and no one would be saved.

sayings.text: He who sits in solitude and is quiet hath escaped from three wars: hearing, speaking, seeing; but against one thing shall he continually battle: that is, his own heart.

cite.searched: Searched the library: not found. The archaic wording may be Helen Waddell's (The Desert Fathers, 1936), whose copyright standing wants checking, or Budge's (1907); neither is in the app.

sayings.text: If a man does not say in his heart, in the world there is only myself and God, he will not gain peace.

sayings.text: Pray as you can, not as you cannot.

cite.searched: Not found among the sayings of the Desert Fathers in public-domain English. The line is commonly credited to Dom John Chapman, Spiritual Letters (1935), a twentieth-century Benedictine: if so it is neither a saying of the Elders nor public domain.
